name: MathlibAnnex.Analysis.CStarAlgebra.NonUnitalCStarRepresentation.exists_preimage_rankOne_of_singleton
title: Every rank-one operator has an algebra preimage

content.display_title: Every rank-one operator has an algebra preimage
content.one_sentence_role: Turns one represented rank-one projection into every rank-one operator using dense orbits and a closed range.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed, let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ represent the unique unitary-equivalence class of nonzero irreducible $*$-representations. For every $x,y\in H$ there is $a\in A$ such that $$\pi(a)=\theta_{x,y},\qquad \theta_{x,y}(z)=\langle y,z\rangle x.$$
content.assumptions: The vectors $x,y$ are arbitrary, including zero. They need not be unit vectors. The separability assumption concerns $H$. No unit is required in $A$.
content.conclusion: Each rank-one operator belongs to the image of the original algebra, not merely to the image of its unitization.
content.proof_summary: Find one rank-one projection in the range. Use irreducibility to obtain a dense original-algebra orbit, multiply around the projection, and pass to limits in both vectors.
proof_steps: Apply [A rank-one projection in a singleton model](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/RankOneProjection.lean#L76-L99) to the nonzero ordered $A$, separable $H$, and singleton $\pi$. It supplies $p\in A$ and a unit vector $e\in H$ with $\pi(p)=\theta_{e,e}$. In particular $\pi(p)e=e$. The theorem [Faithfulness of a non-unital singleton model](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/Singleton.lean#L34-L94) also gives injectivity of $\pi$.

The dense-orbit step in [One rank-one projection generates all rank-one operators in the range](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/NonUnital/CompactRange.lean#L62-L92) uses irreducibility of the unitized representation. Its orbit of $e\ne0$ is dense; every unitization element has the form $(\lambda,a)$ and acts by $$\widehat\pi(\lambda,a)e=\lambda e+\pi(a)e=\pi(\lambda p+a)e.$$ Thus already $\{\pi(a)e:a\in A\}$ is dense in $H$. This calculation is why the preimages below stay in $A$.

For $a,b\in A$ and $z\in H$, multiplicativity and adjoints give $$\pi(apb^*)z=\pi(a)\theta_{e,e}\pi(b)^*z=\langle e,\pi(b)^*z\rangle\pi(a)e=\langle\pi(b)e,z\rangle\pi(a)e.$$ Hence $\pi(apb^*)=\theta_{\pi(a)e,\pi(b)e}$.

Because $\pi$ is injective, it is isometric and has norm-closed range. Approximate arbitrary $x,y$ by vectors $\pi(a)e,\pi(b)e$ in the dense orbit. The estimates $\|\theta_{u,v}\|\le\|u\|\|v\|$ and $$\|\theta_{u,v}-\theta_{x,y}\|\le\|u-x\|\|v\|+\|x\|\|v-y\|$$ show convergence of the corresponding rank-one operators. Closedness then puts $\theta_{x,y}$ in $\pi(A)$, which is the asserted existence of $a$.
